title: Probability space (cited)
primary_statement: (Omega, F, P) with P a probability measure -- math-probability:probability_space

title: Random variable (cited)
primary_statement: a measurable map X: Omega -> R -- math-probability:random_variable

title: Random vector (cited)
primary_statement: a measurable map into R^k -- math-probability:random_variable

title: CDF (cited)
primary_statement: F_X(x) = P(X <= x) -- math-probability:cdf

title: pmf (cited)
primary_statement: p_X(x) = P(X = x) for discrete X -- math-probability:pmf

title: pdf (cited)
primary_statement: density f_X with P(X in A) = int_A f_X -- math-probability:pdf

title: Joint distribution (cited)
primary_statement: the law of (X_1,...,X_n) on R^n -- math-probability:joint_distribution

title: Marginal distribution (cited)
primary_statement: the law of a coordinate obtained by integrating out the rest -- math-probability:marginal_distribution

title: Conditional distribution (cited)
primary_statement: the law of X given Y = y -- math-probability:conditional_distribution

title: Expectation (cited)
primary_statement: E[X] = int X dP -- math-probability:expectation

title: LOTUS (cited)
primary_statement: E[g(X)] = int g dF_X -- math-probability:lotus

title: Linearity of expectation (cited)
primary_statement: E[aX + bY] = a E[X] + b E[Y] -- math-probability:expectation_linearity

title: Variance (cited)
primary_statement: Var(X) = E[(X - E X)^2] = E[X^2] - (E X)^2 -- math-probability:variance

title: Covariance (cited)
primary_statement: Cov(X,Y) = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y] -- math-probability:covariance

title: Correlation (cited)
primary_statement: rho = Cov(X,Y)/sqrt(Var X Var Y), |rho| <= 1 -- math-probability:correlation

title: Moment generating function (cited)
primary_statement: M_X(t) = E[e^{tX}]; MGFs of independent sums multiply -- math-probability:mgf

title: Characteristic function (cited)
primary_statement: phi_X(t) = E[e^{itX}] -- math-probability:characteristic_function

title: Moment (cited)
primary_statement: the k-th moment E[X^k] -- math-probability:moment

title: Independence of random variables (cited)
primary_statement: joint law factorizes -- math-probability:independence_random_variables

title: i.i.d. sequence (cited)
primary_statement: independent and identically distributed -- math-probability:iid

title: Factorization / E[XY]=E[X]E[Y] (cited)
primary_statement: independent => E[g(X)h(Y)] = E[g(X)]E[h(Y)] -- math-probability:independence_factorization

title: Conditional expectation E[X|G] (cited)
primary_statement: the G-measurable L^2 projection of X -- math-probability:conditional_expectation_abstract

title: Tower property (cited)
primary_statement: E[E[X|G]] = E[X] -- math-probability:tower_property

title: Law of total variance (cited)
primary_statement: Var(X) = E[Var(X|T)] + Var(E[X|T]) -- math-probability:law_of_total_variance

title: Bernoulli(p) (cited)
primary_statement: P(X=1)=p; mean p, variance p(1-p) -- math-probability:bernoulli_distribution

title: Binomial(n,p) (cited)
primary_statement: sum of n iid Bernoulli(p) -- math-probability:binomial_distribution

title: Poisson(lambda) (cited)
primary_statement: mean = variance = lambda -- math-probability:poisson_distribution

title: Uniform(a,b) (cited)
primary_statement: constant density on [a,b] -- math-probability:continuous_uniform_distribution

title: Exponential(lambda) (cited)
primary_statement: memoryless; density lambda e^{-lambda x} -- math-probability:exponential_distribution

title: Gamma(k, theta) (cited)
primary_statement: sum of k iid Exponential; additive in shape -- math-probability:gamma_distribution

title: Beta(a,b) (cited)
primary_statement: conjugate density on [0,1] -- math-probability:beta_distribution

title: Normal(mu, sigma^2) (cited)
primary_statement: Gaussian density -- math-probability:normal_distribution

title: Standard normal N(0,1) (cited)
primary_statement: mean 0, variance 1; CDF Phi -- math-probability:standard_normal

title: Normal affine/sum closure (cited)
primary_statement: aX + b and independent sums of normals are normal -- math-probability:normal_affine_closure

title: Cauchy: no mean (cited)
primary_statement: the sample mean of iid Cauchy is again Cauchy -- math-probability:cauchy_no_mean

title: Convergence almost surely (cited)
primary_statement: X_n -> X with probability 1 -- math-probability:convergence_almost_sure

title: Convergence in probability (cited)
primary_statement: P(|X_n - X| > eps) -> 0 -- math-probability:convergence_in_probability

title: Convergence in distribution (cited)
primary_statement: F_{X_n}(x) -> F_X(x) at continuity points -- math-probability:convergence_in_distribution

title: Weak law of large numbers (cited)
primary_statement: sample mean of iid L^1 -> mean in probability -- math-probability:weak_law_large_numbers

title: Strong law of large numbers (cited)
primary_statement: sample mean of iid L^1 -> mean almost surely -- math-probability:strong_law_large_numbers

title: Central limit theorem (cited)
primary_statement: sqrt(n)(mean_n - mu)/sigma -> N(0,1) in distribution -- math-probability:central_limit_theorem

title: Levy continuity theorem (cited)
primary_statement: pointwise CF convergence <=> convergence in distribution -- math-probability:levy_continuity_theorem

title: Slutsky's theorem (cited)
primary_statement: X_n -> X in d, Y_n -> c in p => X_n + Y_n -> X + c, X_n Y_n -> cX -- math-probability:slutsky_theorem

title: Continuous mapping theorem (cited)
primary_statement: g continuous a.s., X_n -> X => g(X_n) -> g(X) in the same mode -- math-probability:continuous_mapping_theorem

title: Delta method (cited)
primary_statement: sqrt(n)(theta_n - theta) -> N(0,v) => sqrt(n)(g(theta_n) - g(theta)) -> N(0, g'(theta)^2 v) -- math-probability:delta_method

title: Markov's inequality (cited)
primary_statement: P(X >= a) <= E[X]/a for X >= 0, a > 0 -- math-probability:markov_inequality

title: Chebyshev's inequality (cited)
primary_statement: P(|X - mu| >= k sigma) <= 1/k^2 -- math-probability:chebyshev_inequality

title: Jensen's inequality (cited)
primary_statement: phi convex => phi(E X) <= E[phi(X)] -- math-probability:jensen_inequality

title: Cauchy-Schwarz for expectation (cited)
primary_statement: E[XY]^2 <= E[X^2] E[Y^2] -- math-probability:cauchy_schwarz_expectation

title: Hoeffding's inequality (cited)
primary_statement: bounded iid: P(mean - E mean >= t) <= exp(-2 n t^2 / range^2) -- math-probability:hoeffding_inequality

title: Continuity (cited)
primary_statement: epsilon-delta continuity of a real function -- math-real-analysis:continuity

title: Differentiability (cited)
primary_statement: existence of the derivative / gradient -- math-real-analysis:differentiation

title: Taylor's theorem with remainder (cited)
primary_statement: f(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a) + ... + R_n, R_n Lagrange form -- math-real-analysis:taylor_theorem

title: Mean value theorem (cited)
primary_statement: f(b) - f(a) = f'(c)(b - a) for some c in (a,b) -- math-real-analysis:mean_value_theorem

title: Compactness / extreme value (cited)
primary_statement: a continuous function on a compact set attains its max -- math-real-analysis:compactness

title: Convex function (cited)
primary_statement: f(tx+(1-t)y) <= t f(x) + (1-t) f(y) -- math-real-analysis:convex_function

title: Differentiate under the integral (cited)
primary_statement: dominated derivative => d/dtheta int f = int d/dtheta f -- math-real-analysis:interchange_limit_integral

title: Finite-dimensional linear algebra (cited, no capsule)
primary_statement: vector space, rank, transpose, inverse, symmetric and PSD matrices, spectral theorem, orthogonal projection and its matrix, trace, quadratic forms

title: Statistical model
primary_statement: a family P = { P_theta : theta in Theta } of candidate distributions for the data

title: Parametric model
primary_statement: a statistical model indexed by a finite-dimensional Theta subset of R^d

title: Parameter space
primary_statement: the set Theta of admissible parameter values

title: Identifiability
primary_statement: theta != theta' => P_theta != P_theta' (the map theta -> P_theta is injective)

title: Dominated family
primary_statement: every P_theta has a density f(x; theta) w.r.t. one common sigma-finite measure

title: i.i.d. sample
primary_statement: X_1,...,X_n drawn independently from one P_theta in the model

title: Statistic
primary_statement: T = T(X_1,...,X_n), a measurable function of the data not depending on theta

title: Likelihood function
primary_statement: L(theta) = prod_i f(x_i; theta), viewed as a function of theta for fixed data

title: Log-likelihood
primary_statement: ell(theta) = sum_i log f(x_i; theta)

title: Score function
primary_statement: U(theta) = d ell / d theta = sum_i d/dtheta log f(x_i; theta)

title: Fisher information (scalar)
primary_statement: I(theta) = Var_theta(U_1(theta)) for one observation

title: Fisher information matrix
primary_statement: I(theta) = Cov_theta(nabla log f(X;theta)), a d x d PSD matrix

title: Score has mean zero
primary_statement: E_theta[U(theta)] = 0 under regularity

title: Information equality
primary_statement: I(theta) = Var_theta(U_1) = -E_theta[ d^2/dtheta^2 log f(X;theta) ]

title: Support does not depend on theta
primary_statement: { x : f(x; theta) > 0 } is the same set for every theta

title: Interchange of derivative and integral
primary_statement: d/dtheta int f(x;theta) dx = int d/dtheta f(x;theta) dx holds (dominated derivative)

title: True parameter is interior
primary_statement: theta_0 lies in the interior of Theta (not on the boundary)

title: Fisher information positive definite
primary_statement: I(theta_0) is finite and positive definite

title: Log-likelihood is smooth
primary_statement: log f(x; theta) is C^3 in theta with locally dominated third derivative

title: Exponential family
primary_statement: f(x; eta) = h(x) exp( eta . T(x) - A(eta) )

title: Natural parameter space
primary_statement: { eta : int h(x) exp(eta . T(x)) dx < inf }, a convex set

title: Cumulant (log-partition) function
primary_statement: A(eta) = log int h(x) exp(eta . T(x)) dx

title: Mean-value parametrization
primary_statement: the reparametrization by mu = E_eta[T(X)] = grad A(eta)

title: Cumulant derivatives give moments
primary_statement: grad A(eta) = E_eta[T(X)], Hess A(eta) = Cov_eta(T(X))

title: T is sufficient in an exponential family
primary_statement: in f(x;eta) = h(x) exp(eta.T(x) - A(eta)), T(X_1..X_n) = sum T(X_i) is sufficient for eta

title: Full-rank exponential family is complete
primary_statement: if the natural parameter space contains an open set, the natural sufficient statistic is complete

title: Sufficient statistic
primary_statement: T is sufficient for theta if the conditional law of the data given T does not depend on theta

title: Neyman-Fisher factorization
primary_statement: T is sufficient iff f(x;theta) = g(T(x); theta) h(x) for some g, h >= 0

title: Minimal sufficient statistic
primary_statement: a sufficient statistic that is a function of every other sufficient statistic

title: Ancillary statistic
primary_statement: a statistic whose distribution does not depend on theta

title: Complete statistic
primary_statement: E_theta[g(T)] = 0 for all theta implies g(T) = 0 a.s. for all theta

title: Bounded completeness
primary_statement: the completeness condition restricted to bounded g

title: Basu's theorem
primary_statement: a complete sufficient statistic is independent of every ancillary statistic

title: Estimator
primary_statement: a statistic theta_hat = theta_hat(X_1..X_n) used as a guess for theta (or for g(theta))

title: Bias
primary_statement: b(theta) = E_theta[theta_hat] - theta

title: Mean squared error
primary_statement: MSE(theta) = E_theta[(theta_hat - theta)^2]

title: Bias-variance decomposition
primary_statement: MSE(theta) = Var_theta(theta_hat) + b(theta)^2

title: Unbiased estimator
primary_statement: E_theta[theta_hat] = theta for every theta

title: Consistency
primary_statement: theta_hat_n -> theta in probability (under P_theta) for every theta

title: Asymptotic variance
primary_statement: v(theta) with sqrt(n)(theta_hat_n - theta) -> N(0, v(theta)) in distribution

title: Asymptotically normal estimator
primary_statement: sqrt(n)(theta_hat_n - theta) converges in distribution to a centered normal

title: Asymptotic relative efficiency
primary_statement: ratio of asymptotic variances of two estimators of the same quantity

title: Asymptotic efficiency
primary_statement: an estimator whose asymptotic variance equals the Cramer-Rao bound I(theta)^{-1}

title: UMVUE
primary_statement: an unbiased estimator with the smallest variance for every theta among all unbiased estimators

title: Cramer-Rao lower bound
primary_statement: Var_theta(theta_hat) >= (1 + b'(theta))^2 / (n I(theta)); = 1/(n I(theta)) if unbiased

title: Rao-Blackwell theorem
primary_statement: if T is sufficient, E[theta_hat | T] is unbiased (if theta_hat was) with Var no larger

title: Lehmann-Scheffe theorem
primary_statement: an unbiased function of a complete sufficient statistic is the unique UMVUE

title: CRLB attained iff exponential family
primary_statement: an unbiased estimator attains the CRLB for all theta iff the model is a one-parameter exponential family and theta_hat is its natural sufficient statistic

title: Method of moments
primary_statement: solve the first d population-moment equations E_theta[X^k] = (1/n) sum X_i^k for theta

title: Plug-in principle
primary_statement: estimate a functional T(P) by T(P_hat_n) with P_hat_n the empirical distribution

title: Maximum likelihood estimator
primary_statement: theta_hat = argmax_theta L(theta) = argmax_theta ell(theta)

title: MLE solves the score equation
primary_statement: an interior MLE satisfies U(theta_hat) = 0

title: MLE invariance
primary_statement: if theta_hat is the MLE of theta then g(theta_hat) is the MLE of g(theta)

title: MLE consistency
primary_statement: under identifiability and regularity, theta_hat_n -> theta_0 in probability

title: MLE asymptotic normality
primary_statement: sqrt(n)(theta_hat_n - theta_0) -> N(0, I(theta_0)^{-1}) in distribution

title: M-estimator
primary_statement: theta_hat maximizes (1/n) sum m(X_i; theta), or solves (1/n) sum psi(X_i; theta) = 0

title: Sandwich (robust) variance
primary_statement: an M-estimator has asymptotic variance A^{-1} B A^{-T} with A = -E[psi'], B = E[psi psi^T]

title: Bayes estimator
primary_statement: the decision rule minimizing the posterior expected loss E[ L(theta, a) | x ]

title: Posterior mean under squared loss
primary_statement: under L(theta,a) = (theta - a)^2 the Bayes estimator is E[theta | x]

title: Posterior median under absolute loss
primary_statement: under L(theta,a) = |theta - a| the Bayes estimator is a posterior median

title: Conjugate prior
primary_statement: a prior family closed under the likelihood: posterior stays in the family

title: Credible interval
primary_statement: a set C(x) with posterior probability P(theta in C(x) | x) = 1 - alpha

title: Bernstein-von Mises theorem
primary_statement: under regularity the posterior is asymptotically N(theta_hat, (n I)^{-1}); credible sets have frequentist coverage

title: Loss function
primary_statement: L(theta, a) >= 0, the cost of action a when the truth is theta

title: Risk function
primary_statement: R(theta, delta) = E_theta[ L(theta, delta(X)) ]

title: Decision rule
primary_statement: delta: data -> action space (an estimator or a test is a decision rule)

title: Admissibility
primary_statement: delta is admissible if no rule has R(theta, .) <= R(theta, delta) everywhere with strict somewhere

title: Minimax rule
primary_statement: a rule minimizing sup_theta R(theta, delta)

title: Bayes risk
primary_statement: r(pi, delta) = int R(theta, delta) pi(dtheta) for a prior pi

title: Bayes rule minimizes Bayes risk pointwise
primary_statement: the rule minimizing the posterior expected loss for each x minimizes r(pi, .)

title: Complete class theorem
primary_statement: under convexity/compactness the Bayes rules (and their limits) form a complete class

title: James-Stein: MLE inadmissible in dimension >= 3
primary_statement: for X ~ N(theta, I_d), d >= 3, the shrinkage estimator dominates X in total squared-error risk

title: Chi-squared distribution
primary_statement: chi^2_k := Gamma(k/2, 1/2); equivalently the law of sum of k iid N(0,1)^2

title: Student's t distribution
primary_statement: t_k := Z / sqrt(V/k) with Z ~ N(0,1) independent of V ~ chi^2_k

title: F distribution
primary_statement: F_{d1,d2} := (U/d1)/(V/d2) with U ~ chi^2_{d1} independent of V ~ chi^2_{d2}

title: Chi-squared degrees of freedom add
primary_statement: independent chi^2_a + chi^2_b = chi^2_{a+b}

title: Sample mean
primary_statement: Xbar_n = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n X_i

title: Sample variance is unbiased
primary_statement: E[S^2] = sigma^2 for any distribution with finite variance (the n-1 divisor)

title: Xbar and S^2 are independent for a normal sample
primary_statement: if X_1..X_n ~ iid N(mu, sigma^2) then Xbar and S^2 are independent

title: (n-1)S^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_{n-1}
primary_statement: for an iid normal sample, (n-1)S^2/sigma^2 has the chi-squared law with n-1 df

title: The t-statistic has Student's t law
primary_statement: sqrt(n)(Xbar - mu)/S ~ t_{n-1} for an iid N(mu, sigma^2) sample

title: Cochran's theorem
primary_statement: if sum of quadratic forms Q_i in iid standard normals sums to |x|^2 with ranks summing to n, the Q_i are independent chi^2_{r_i}

title: ANOVA sum-of-squares decomposition
primary_statement: total SS = between-group SS + within-group SS, with matching degrees of freedom

title: One-sample t-test
primary_statement: reject H0: mu = mu_0 when |sqrt(n)(Xbar - mu_0)/S| > t_{n-1, 1-alpha/2}; exact level alpha

title: Two-sample t-test
primary_statement: pooled or Welch t-statistic for H0: mu_X = mu_Y

title: F-test for equality of variances
primary_statement: S_X^2 / S_Y^2 ~ F_{n-1, m-1} under H0: sigma_X = sigma_Y for normal samples

title: Confidence set
primary_statement: C(X) with P_theta(theta in C(X)) >= 1 - alpha for every theta

title: Coverage probability
primary_statement: P_theta(theta in C(X)) as a function of theta

title: Pivotal quantity
primary_statement: Q(X, theta) whose distribution does not depend on theta

title: Pivot method for a confidence set
primary_statement: invert P(a <= Q(X, theta) <= b) = 1 - alpha to a set of theta

title: Duality of confidence sets and tests
primary_statement: C(x) = { theta_0 : the level-alpha test of H0: theta = theta_0 accepts at x } has coverage 1 - alpha, and conversely

title: z-interval for a normal mean
primary_statement: Xbar +- z_{1-alpha/2} sigma/sqrt(n) has exact coverage 1 - alpha when sigma is known

title: t-interval for a normal mean
primary_statement: Xbar +- t_{n-1,1-alpha/2} S/sqrt(n) has exact coverage 1 - alpha

title: Chi-squared interval for a normal variance
primary_statement: ((n-1)S^2/chi^2_{n-1,1-alpha/2}, (n-1)S^2/chi^2_{n-1,alpha/2}) has exact coverage

title: Wald confidence interval
primary_statement: theta_hat +- z_{1-alpha/2} se(theta_hat) with se from the estimated information; asymptotic coverage

title: Delta-method standard error
primary_statement: se(g(theta_hat)) = |g'(theta_hat)| se(theta_hat); gives an asymptotic interval for g(theta)

title: Large-sample Wald interval from the MLE
primary_statement: theta_hat_MLE +- z_{1-alpha/2} / sqrt(n I(theta_hat)) has coverage -> 1 - alpha

title: Null hypothesis
primary_statement: H0: theta in Theta_0, the hypothesis put on trial

title: Alternative hypothesis
primary_statement: H1: theta in Theta_1 = Theta \ Theta_0

title: Test function
primary_statement: phi: data -> [0,1], the probability of rejecting H0 given the data

title: Size (and level) of a test
primary_statement: size = sup_{theta in Theta_0} E_theta[phi]; a level-alpha test has size <= alpha

title: Power function
primary_statement: beta(theta) = E_theta[phi], the rejection probability; power on Theta_1

title: Type I and Type II error
primary_statement: Type I: reject a true H0 (prob <= size); Type II: fail to reject a false H0 (prob 1 - power)

title: Neyman-Pearson lemma
primary_statement: for H0: f0 vs H1: f1 the size-alpha likelihood-ratio test phi* = 1{f1 > k f0} is most powerful

title: Monotone likelihood ratio
primary_statement: f(x; theta1)/f(x; theta0) is nondecreasing in a statistic T(x) whenever theta1 > theta0

title: Karlin-Rubin theorem
primary_statement: under MLR in T, the test 1{T > c} is UMP for H0: theta <= theta_0 vs H1: theta > theta_0

title: Likelihood ratio test
primary_statement: reject H0 for small Lambda = sup_{Theta_0} L / sup_{Theta} L

title: Wilks' theorem
primary_statement: under H0 and regularity, -2 log Lambda -> chi^2_r in distribution, r = dim drop

title: Wald test
primary_statement: reject when (theta_hat - theta_0)^2 n I(theta_hat) exceeds chi^2_{1,1-alpha}

title: Score (Rao) test
primary_statement: reject when U(theta_0)^2 / (n I(theta_0)) exceeds chi^2_{1,1-alpha}; needs only the null fit

title: Wald, score, and LR tests are asymptotically equivalent
primary_statement: under H0 and local alternatives the three statistics differ by o_p(1) and share the chi^2_r limit

title: p-value
primary_statement: the smallest alpha at which the observed data reject H0; p(X) = sup_{Theta_0} P_theta(T >= T(x))

title: p-value is uniform under a simple null
primary_statement: for a continuous test statistic with a simple H0, p(X) ~ Uniform(0,1) under H0

title: Pearson chi-squared goodness of fit
primary_statement: sum (O_j - E_j)^2 / E_j -> chi^2_{k-1-d} under the fitted null

title: Family-wise error rate
primary_statement: FWER = P(at least one true null rejected) across a family of m tests

title: Bonferroni correction
primary_statement: testing each of m hypotheses at level alpha/m controls FWER at alpha

title: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control
primary_statement: the step-up rule on ordered p-values controls the false discovery rate at alpha under independence

title: Empirical CDF
primary_statement: F_hat_n(x) = (1/n) sum 1{X_i <= x}

title: Order statistic
primary_statement: X_(1) <= ... <= X_(n), the sorted sample

title: Sample quantile
primary_statement: F_hat_n^{-1}(p), a plug-in estimate of the population quantile

title: Glivenko-Cantelli theorem
primary_statement: sup_x |F_hat_n(x) - F(x)| -> 0 almost surely, for every F

title: DKW inequality
primary_statement: P(sup_x |F_hat_n(x) - F(x)| > t) <= 2 exp(-2 n t^2); a distribution-free confidence band

title: Plug-in estimator of a functional
primary_statement: T(F_hat_n) for a statistical functional T

title: The bootstrap
primary_statement: approximate the sampling distribution of T(X_1..X_n) by resampling with replacement from F_hat_n

title: Bootstrap consistency
primary_statement: for a Hadamard-differentiable functional the bootstrap distribution converges to the sampling distribution

title: Kernel density estimator
primary_statement: f_hat_h(x) = (1/nh) sum K((x - X_i)/h)

title: KDE bias-variance / bandwidth tradeoff
primary_statement: bias = O(h^2), variance = O(1/(nh)); MISE-optimal h ~ n^{-1/5} gives rate n^{-4/5}

title: Gaussian linear model
primary_statement: y = X beta + eps, X in R^{n x p} fixed full-rank, eps ~ N(0, sigma^2 I_n)

title: Ordinary least squares
primary_statement: beta_hat = argmin_b |y - X b|^2

title: Normal equations
primary_statement: X^T X beta_hat = X^T y; beta_hat = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T y

title: OLS fitted values are an orthogonal projection
primary_statement: y_hat = H y with H = X(X^T X)^{-1} X^T the projection onto the column space of X

title: Residual sum of squares
primary_statement: RSS = |y - X beta_hat|^2 = y^T (I - H) y

title: Unbiased estimator of the error variance
primary_statement: sigma_hat^2 = RSS / (n - p) has E[sigma_hat^2] = sigma^2

title: Gauss-Markov theorem
primary_statement: among linear unbiased estimators of c^T beta, OLS has the smallest variance (BLUE), needing only E[eps]=0, Cov(eps)=sigma^2 I

title: Distribution of the OLS estimator
primary_statement: under normal errors beta_hat ~ N(beta, sigma^2 (X^T X)^{-1}) and is independent of RSS

title: t-test for a regression coefficient
primary_statement: (beta_hat_j - beta_j) / se(beta_hat_j) ~ t_{n-p} under normal errors

title: F-test for a linear hypothesis
primary_statement: ((RSS_0 - RSS)/q) / (RSS/(n-p)) ~ F_{q, n-p} under the reduced-model null

title: Coefficient of determination
primary_statement: R^2 = 1 - RSS/TSS, the fraction of variance explained

title: Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem
primary_statement: the OLS coefficient on X_2 equals that from regressing residualized y on residualized X_2

title: Likelihood principle
primary_statement: inference should depend on the data only through the likelihood function; Birnbaum: sufficiency + conditionality => likelihood principle

title: Sufficiency principle
primary_statement: if T is sufficient and T(x) = T(y) then x and y yield the same inference

title: Conditionality principle
primary_statement: if a randomly chosen experiment is performed, inference should condition on which experiment was run

title: Local asymptotic normality (boundary)
primary_statement: regular models are locally asymptotically normal; the log-likelihood ratio has a Gaussian-shift limit

title: Hajek convolution theorem (boundary)
primary_statement: the limit law of any regular estimator is the efficient normal convolved with independent noise

title: Local asymptotic minimax bound (boundary)
primary_statement: the local minimax risk of any estimator is bounded below by the efficient (CRLB) risk

title: Donsker's theorem (boundary)
primary_statement: the empirical process sqrt(n)(F_hat_n - F) converges to a Brownian bridge

title: Minimax rates of convergence (boundary)
